subject: Archaeology
title: Zooarchaeology: Reading Animal Bones
description: Learn Zooarchaeology: Reading Animal Bones in one minute.

hook.text: The animal bones in ancient trash heaps reveal what people ate, what they farmed, and how they treated their animals.

buildup.text: Zooarchaeologists identify species, age at death, butchery marks, and signs of disease from bone fragments.

discovery.text: Domesticated animals have smaller bones than wild ancestors. Tracking size changes reveals when domestication happened.

twist.text: Cut marks on human bones at some sites reveal cannibalism. Animal bone experts are often the ones who spot the evidence.

climax.text: At Jamestown colony, horse and dog bones show butchery marks — proof the settlers ate their animals during the starving time.

punchline.text: Trash tells the truth. What people threw away reveals what they could not admit.

quiz.question: How do zooarchaeologists detect animal domestication?
options: Domesticated animals have different colored bones
Domesticated animals have smaller bones than their wild ancestors
Domesticated animals are always found inside structures

details.summary: Zooarchaeology studies animal remains from archaeological sites to reconstruct past human diets, animal husbandry, hunting practices, and environmental conditions.
details.whyItMatters: Animal bones are among the most common finds at archaeological sites. Zooarchaeology transforms these fragments into detailed evidence about ancient diets, farming systems, trade, ritual practices, and environmental exploitation.
takeaways: Studies animal bones to reconstruct past diets and economies
Identifies species, age, sex, and butchery patterns on bones

faq.question: What can animal bones tell us about ancient people?
faq.answer: Species ratios reveal whether people hunted, herded, or fished. Kill-off patterns show herd management strategies. Butchery marks indicate meat processing techniques. Pathologies reveal working animals versus food animals. Exotic species document trade networks and status display.

faq.question: How do zooarchaeologists identify fragmentary bones?
faq.answer: Training with modern reference collections is essential. Specialists learn to identify species from small fragments by surface texture, cortical thickness, and diagnostic features. Digital databases now assist identification.
